name: Jeshaiah
overview: Jeshaiah was a male Levite, distinguished as the son of Jeduthun and set apart among the musicians in the service of the temple. He was chosen eighth by lot to be one of the singers who prophesied through musical instruments such as lyres, harps, and cymbals. His role highlights the importance of worship and prophetic music within the Levitical duties.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshaiah means 'YHWH will save,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in God's saving power. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries significant spiritual implication as recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jeshaiah as the son of Jeduthun, a notable figure connected to temple music. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshaiah's significance lies in his role as one of the Levite singers chosen by lot to prophesy through music, demonstrating the God-ordained function of worship in Israel. Being the eighth chosen among the singers emphasizes the ordered and divinely guided nature of temple worship. His service with musical instruments like lyres, harps, and cymbals underscores the integral role of music in the spiritual life of Israel as recorded in 1 Chronicles 25.
